text: ← Foundations contents THE LEARNING PATH WHAT YOU WILL LEARNSolve detailed balance for uν and identify where the denominator’s −1 comes from. 01Specify the quantity to be found uν is radiation energy density per unit frequency, in J m⁻³ Hz⁻¹. A narrow interval Δν contains approximately uνΔν of energy density. The two levels are separated by hν; n₁ and n₂ are their number densities and g₁ and g₂ their statistical weights. Our B coefficients multiply uν. Coefficients defined to multiply the mean intensity Jν have different numerical values. We assume a narrow line across which uν is nearly constant. 02Write down the three processes Absorption: n₁B₁₂uν. Spontaneous emission: n₂A₂₁. Stimulated emission: n₂B₂₁uν. When atoms and radiation share thermal equilibrium, the upward and downward transition rates balance. n1B12uν = n2A21 + n2B21uν 03Collect the uν terms and divide (n1B12−n2B21)uν = n2A21 uν = A21/B21(n1/n2)(B12/B21)−1 In the second line we divided numerator and denominator by n₂B₂₁. So far this only rearranges the balance condition; it does not yet determine the spectrum. 04Insert the Boltzmann ratio and Einstein relations n1n2 = g1g2ehν/(kBT), g1B12 = g2B21 A21B21 = 8πhν3c3 The B relation reflects microscopic transition symmetry. The A/B ratio is linked to electromagnetic mode counting and can also be fixed by matching the classical Rayleigh–Jeans limit. These are additional physical inputs; detailed balance alone does not determine the factor 8π. 05Arrive at Planck’s law uν(T) = 8πhν3c31exp(hν/kBT)−1 At low frequency, x = hν/(kBT) ≪ 1 and eˣ − 1 ≈ x. Substitution gives uν ≈ 8πν²kBT/c³, the Rayleigh–Jeans result. At high frequency the exponential suppresses the spectrum. Bν = c4πuν For isotropic thermal radiation. Specific intensity Bν, energy density uν, and surface flux have different units. CHECK YOUR UNDERSTANDING Pause and work it out. Which of the three processes produces the “−1” in the final denominator? Show the answer and reasoning Stimulated emission. It comes from the second term in n₁B₁₂ − n₂B₂₁, absorption minus stimulated emission.
